analysis: The change set is documentation-only: docs/developer/test.md. The bumped date (2026-11-04 to 2026-11-05) and the shard and CI-caching prose appear in head lines 3 and 115-166. Further hunks in the file (base ~1210-1313, 1885, 2219) lie outside the supplied excerpts and could not be examined. The edits visible in the patch describe how CI shards run provider tests: build-once products, a lock-retry rule, an audit warning for unweighted serial suites, and a wording change on the build cache. The supplied base units (lines 2767-3239, test docs for MiMo, Qwen TP and cluster checks) and the head lines 1-455 contain no executable code, secrets or configuration. I checked them against the threat model: no change touches the provider-to-coordinator WebSocket (TB-002), attestation (TB-009, TB-011), cache crypto and TTL (T-041), the fan helper (TB-010), the add-on hold socket (TB-012), or the installer and gpu-limit boundaries (TB-013, TB-014). The prefix-cache text mentions only the SSD test working volume selector (DARKBLOOM_SSD_TEST_TMPDIR) in the test docs, and says explicitly that production free-space checks, write limits and cleanup still apply. It does not change the cache policy, so T-041 mitigations are not affected. The documented lock-retry rule reruns a selection only when its log proves every test passed. This is CI-process guidance and weakens no production control. Limits: the patch excerpt is truncated, and the changed ranges listed for the 1200-2250 region were not supplied as source units. Any security-relevant claims in those hunks, and the referenced scripts (scripts/swift_test_lock_retry.py, scripts/provider-test-shards.py), were not visible. Nothing observed indicates a regression.
